stories.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with 15-second video
paragraphs: Google said on Nov. 5, 2026, that Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is generally available on the Gemini API and Google Cloud. The update adds native clips up to 15 seconds (up from 10 on Omni 1.1), multi-turn conversational editing, stronger reference adherence, and a 30% price cut to $0.07 per second for 720p.

According to Google DeepMind product manager Anish Nangia, users can draft at 360p or 720p, refine with follow-up edits instead of full regenerations, then upscale selected clips to 1080p or 4K, and set duration in one-second steps from 3 to 15 seconds.

Google says the model keeps character and product details more consistent across camera moves, supports short motion references up to three seconds plus audio cues, improves multi-speaker lip-sync, and watermarks outputs with SynthID. Provisioned Throughput is available for enterprise customers.

stories.title: OpenAI introduces Images 2.6 with Flare, Sunburst, GIFs, and SVG export
paragraphs: MarkTechPost reports that OpenAI shipped Images 2.6 on Nov. 4, 2026, across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, saying generation is 50% faster than before and that users now create more than 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT and the API.

According to MarkTechPost's summary of the launch, the API adds GPT-Image-2.6 Flare for fast iteration—returning images in as little as six seconds at low quality—and GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst for higher detail and stronger edit consistency. ChatGPT users can create animated GIFs, edit frames, and save reusable reference images.

MarkTechPost also lists markup-guided edits, SVG export, GIF output, and a complexity parameter (low, medium, or high; default high) separate from quality, with token pricing matching the prior image release.

stories.title: Mistral expands Studio for enterprise agents, workflows, and apps alongside Le Chonk
paragraphs: Mistral AI said it is expanding Mistral Studio with managed agents and apps, plus updates for workflows, enterprise context, observability, and evaluations. The company positions Studio as the platform for putting Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) to work on coding, defensive cybersecurity, and document reasoning tasks.

According to Mistral, Studio can run in the cloud, a customer's VPC, on-premises, or mixed environments. Developers can build agents with skills, code sandboxes, subagents, and approval hooks; define workflows with event triggers and a visual graph; and host apps with authentication and access controls. A Mistral MCP server lets developers test locally and deploy with one command.

Mistral cites production customers including ABANCA, Accenture, Alten, BNP Paribas, Capgemini, CMA CGM, and Tata Consultancy Services. Internal examples include an incident-investigation agent that follows runbooks and posts findings in Slack, and a product-ops workflow that Mistral says saves about 35 hours a week routing feedback.
